gen-megrim-gf-hind-guntur: Sharp, sci-fi angles lead the way in Megrim, drawn with strokes that never swell or thin. Hind Guntur sits underneath as a plain sans, tall in the lowercase and wide between curve ends and stems.
gen-megrim-gf-hind-madurai: Futuristic from the first glyph, Megrim cuts its letters at a single measured thickness. Hind Madurai follows with lowercase that fills the line almost like capitals, and its s curves open wide at both ends.
gen-megrim-gf-hind-mysuru: Angular and a bit sci-fi, Megrim sets its measured strokes against a body that feels thoroughly contemporary and businesslike. Hind Mysuru keeps its tall sans lowercase smooth, with no thinning.
gen-megrim-gf-hind-siliguri: Megrim arrives all angles and future-tense, every stroke cut to one measured thickness. Hind Siliguri then hums along in sans-serif at a constant line weight, its rounds gapped open and its capitals rising gently above the small letters.
gen-megrim-gf-hind-vadodara: Megrim's most striking habit is its stroke, which ends at one measured thickness, giving angular futuristic letters. And Hind Vadodara, a sans with spacious terminal gaps and tall open bowls, does the quiet work of making text easy to take in.
gen-megrim-gf-huninn: Huninn reads modern and businesslike, its s terminals held clear of the body and its lowercase rising close to cap height. Megrim is the sharper partner, and its angular, futuristic strokes give the sans-serif below a striking contrast.
gen-megrim-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight brings short ascenders and curve tails held back from the body, like bent tubing. And Megrim, angular and futuristic at one measured thickness, supplies the sharpest contrast in the pair.
gen-megrim-gf-karla: Megrim's strokes never change width, and that gives its angular, futuristic letters a drawn-with-a-ruler feel. But Karla, a sans-serif with a gaping c and a tall middle band, is the one that feels sturdy and approachable.
gen-megrim-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri is a plain sans with rounded letters that stay open and inviting. Megrim brings the opposite character, angular and futuristic, and Kedebideri's tall lowercase sets that off nicely.
gen-megrim-gf-krub: Futuristic angles, no thick or thin anywhere: that's Megrim. Krub lets a pronounced x-height and pen-lifted curves soften the sans-serif text, so the page moves from sharp, bold display letters into something more contemporary and relaxed.
